answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a public randomness beacon, e.g. dune, canyon, or crystal, woven into a fresh task. Because the word is unpredictable until the epoch opens, an attacker cannot precompute template answers or spin up thousands of sockpuppets in advance; every identity must actually solve a novel task in real time. Work scales linearly with identities while legitimate agents solve one challenge each. Sybil cost: one genuine solve plus compute and latency per fake identity, making mass fake accounts uneconomical.
